statement: Let n = len(arr) and define M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v, where min is the ordinary integer minimum. The function returns a result r (an integer) such that: (a) r >= 0; (b) for every integer v with 0 <= v, |M(r) - target| <= |M(v) - target|; (c) for every integer v with 0 <= v and |M(v) - target| = |M(r) - target|, r <= v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail on any input satisfying the preconditions (no panic, no out-of-bounds access, and no arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let maxarr = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i]. The returned value r satisfies 0 <= r <= min(target, maxarr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Suppose there is an integer c such that arr[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) (so 1 <= c <= 100000). Let n = len(arr), q = floor(target / n) (integer division), and rem = target - q*n. If target >= n*c then r = c; if target < n*c then r = q when 2*rem <= n, and r = q + 1 when 2*rem > n.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: If target <= len(arr), then r = 0 when 2*target <= len(arr), and r = 1 when 2*target > len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let total = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} arr[i] and maxarr = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i]. If total <= target, then r = maxarr.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let maxarr = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i] and M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v. If r < maxarr, then M(r + 1) > target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v. If r > 0, then M(r - 1) < target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let maxarr = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i] and M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v. If there exists an integer v with 0 <= v <= maxarr and M(v) = target, then M(r) = target, and for every integer v with 0 <= v <= maxarr and v != r it holds that M(v) != target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: For every slice arr2 with len(arr2) = len(arr) for which there exists a permutation pi of {0, 1, ..., len(arr)-1} such that arr2[i] = arr[pi(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), the value returned by find_best_value on (arr2, target) equals the value returned by find_best_value on (arr, target).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let maxarr = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i] and M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v. Let v0 be the largest integer v with 0 <= v <= maxarr and M(v) <= target (it exists because M(0) = 0 <= target). Then either (v0 = maxarr and r = v0), or (v0 < maxarr and (r = v0 or r = v0 + 1)).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v and let total = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} arr[i]. If target <= total, then 2 * |M(r) - target| <= len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v. If M(r) >= target, then for every integer v with 0 <= v < r, M(v) < target; equivalently, r is the smallest integer v with 0 <= v and M(v) >= target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v) for an integer v. If M(r) > target, then target - M(r - 1) > M(r) - target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let r be the returned value. Then r = 0 if and only if 2 * target <= len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.

statement: Let maxarr = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i], M(v) = sum_{i=0}^{len(arr)-1} min(arr[i], v), and let v0 be the largest integer v with 0 <= v <= maxarr and M(v) <= target. Then v0 exists. If v0 = maxarr, r = v0. If v0 < maxarr, put a = target - M(v0) and b = M(v0+1) - target; then a >= 0, b > 0, and r = v0 when a <= b, while r = v0+1 when a > b.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000, and 1 <= target <= 100000.
